- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% or apply downward bias to avoid “overshoot” after sharp spikes.
- Model frequently lags in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast horizon); apply slight upward bias to early days if sentiment is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a peak too early; cap forecast at 1–2 days after peak or reduce slope.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.2) triggers model overcorrection; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast adjustment magnitude by 50%.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are often too conservative; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- Avoid “forecast drift” — if model consistently forecasts 2–3% higher than true outcome over 30d, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next horizon.
